## Autoregressive Facts

Some facts about `em:

1. An AR(1) model is stationary^[Technically we should say "asymptotically stationary" depending on what we assume in regard to the initial conditions.] for $|\beta_1| < 1$ with mean
$$
\mu = E(Y_t) = \beta_0/(1-\beta_1) 
$$
and autocorrelation
$$
\rho_k = \beta_1^k
$$
2. The coefficients $\beta_0,\beta_1$ can be estimated in a manner similar to OLS, but (assuming stationarity) the answers are easy to guess. Since 
$$
Cov(Y_t,Y_{t-1}) = \beta_1 Var(Y_{t-1})
$$
we can solve for $\beta_1$ to get 
$$
\beta_1  =  Cov(Y_t,Y_{t-1})/Var(Y_{t-1}) = Corr(Y_t,Y_{t-1}).
$$
Therefore, $\hat{\beta}_1 \approx \rho_1$. Meanwhile, 
$$
\beta_0 = (1-\beta_1) E(Y_t)
$$
so $\hat{\beta_0} \approx (1-\hat{\beta}_1)\bar{y}$. We can verify these observations using `lm` to directly fit a model of $y_t ~ y_{t-1}$ to the unemployment data. 

```{r}
url = "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=UNRATE"

unemployment = read_csv(url) |>
  mutate(observation_date = as.Date(observation_date)) |>
  filter(observation_date>="1980-01-01") |>
  drop_na()
rho_ur=acf(unemployment$UNRATE)
```

```{r}
rho1=rho_ur$acf[2]
ybar=mean(unemployment$UNRATE)

T=length(unemployment$UNRATE)
x=unemployment$UNRATE[1:(T-1)]
y=unemployment$UNRATE[2:T]

ur_lm=lm(y~x)
cat("Coefficients from lm:", coef(ur_lm))

cat("\nCoefficients from theory:",c((1-rho1)*ybar,rho1))
```
